stories.title: Walmart Inks Deal at New Miami-Dade Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Walmart has signed an industrial lease in Miami-Dade County, likely spanning more than 130,000 square feet. The retail giant inked a deal at Seagis Property Group’s newly completed warehouse at 10900 Northwest 138th Street in Medley, facing West Okeechobee Road near the Florida Turnpike, property records show. The 16-year lease includes three five-year extensions. Public documents suggest the tenant will occupy the entire 130,150-square-foot property, which rises 40 feet tall and includes two drive-in doors and 46 dock-high doors. A spokesperson for Walmart declined to comment. A representative for the landlord did not respond to requests for comment. Seagis Property Group completed the warehouse this year after buying the 13.2-acre site for $17.5 million in 2022. In another recent South Florida deal, Bentonville, Ark.-based Walmart bought a 24-acre parcel in Palm Beach County for $11.7 million in August to build a superstore. Walmart also renewed its 83,342-square-foot industrial lease at 1981 North Powerline Road in Pompano Beach late last year, according to a market report from Cushman & Wakefield. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Walmart leased 130,150 SF warehouse in Miami-Dade (Medley) for 16 years plus extensions.
Seagis completed new facility; Walmart also bought 24-acre Palm Beach parcel for $11.7M in August.
Lease signals sustained e-commerce/logistics demand in South Florida industrial corridor near Turnpike.
stories.summary: Walmart signed a 16-year lease (with three 5-year extensions) on a newly completed 130,150-square-foot warehouse at 10900 Northwest 138th Street in Medley, Miami-Dade County, appearing to occupy the entire property. The deal follows Walmart's August purchase of a 24-acre parcel in Palm Beach County for $11.7 million to build a superstore. This represents continued major retailer investment in South Florida's logistics infrastructure.
stories.impact: Walmart's dual commitment (lease + land buy) in South Florida signals sustained confidence in the region's last-mile logistics and population density, underpinning long-term warehouse-driven employment. While primarily industrial, this anchors job creation that supports multifamily demand in adjacent South Florida submarkets (Medley, West Broward corridor); monitor for population inflow and ripple rental growth in nearby residential markets.

stories.title: Core Spaces Delivers 6K Student Housing Beds Across Six Properties
stories.excerpt: Core Spaces announced the delivery of approximately 6,000 new student housing beds across six purpose-built student housing communities, completed ahead of schedule for the 2026 academic year.The new developments further expand Core’s growing national portfolio across university markets. “Six projects at this scale are a big moment for Core, but we’re just getting started,” said Marc Lifshin, co-founder and CEO of Core Spaces. “We’re going all-in on the markets we believe in and continuing to push what student living can and should be: better design, better technology and, most importantly, a better experience.”Projects include Hub Tempe near Arizona State University, ōLiv Columbia near the University of South Carolina, and Hub College Station near Texas A&M. Most recently, Core closed on a $300 million, four-property portfolio for the Core University Living Real Estate Investment Trust, furthering its disciplined approach to growth and capital deployment across Tier 1 markets. The post Core Spaces Delivers 6K Student Housing Beds Across Six Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Core Spaces delivered 6,000 beds across six student housing communities ahead of 2026 schedule.
Projects represent major portfolio expansion; CEO signals continued build-out in selected university markets.
Ahead-of-schedule delivery suggests strong leasing momentum and operational confidence in student housing demand.
stories.summary: Core Spaces completed delivery of approximately 6,000 new student housing beds across six purpose-built communities, ahead of schedule for the 2026 academic year. CEO Marc Lifshin signaled continued aggressive expansion in select university markets with emphasis on design and technology. The announcement marks a significant scaling moment for the operator's national platform.
stories.impact: Ahead-of-schedule student housing delivery indicates strong leasing demand and occupancy confidence in the markets where Core is building. For multifamily developers: this signals continued capital appetite and operational momentum in university-adjacent submarkets; monitor which specific markets Core is targeting, as their confidence may indicate supply gaps or demographic tailwinds (enrollment growth, international student inflow) that could support co-located market-rate and student housing development.

stories.title: Torrington Plans Residential Conversion of Danvers Residence Inn
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $13.5-million sale and financing of the 96-room Residence Inn Boston North Shore/Danvers, an extended-stay hotel with approved conversion rights to an 88-unit multifamily residential community. The property is located at 51 Newbury St. in Danvers, MA, approximately 20 miles north of Boston. JLL represented the seller, an affiliate of PEG Companies, Inc. Torrington acquired the asset and plans to move forward with a multifamily conversion after an initial period of continued hotel operations under the Residence Inn brand. JLL also worked on behalf of Torrington to secure financing for the acquisition. The JLL Capital Markets team included Hotels & Hospitality Senior Managing Director Alan Suzuki and Managing Director Matthew Enright; Managing Directors John Flaherty and Jon Bryant, who represented the multifamily investment perspective; and Associates Michael Schwarze and Anthony Nakhle. The Debt Advisory team that arranged the acquisition financing included Director Michael Shepard, Director Ryan Parker and Associate Hunter Cuthbertson. “The North Shore continues to benefit from its position as a high-barrier suburban alternative to Boston, with strong fundamentals supporting both hospitality and residential demand,” said Suzuki. “Torrington recognized the value in acquiring an income-producing hotel asset with a de-risked pathway to capitalize on severe housing supply constraints and robust rental demand in one of Greater Boston’s most connected suburban markets.” The post Torrington Plans Residential Conversion of Danvers Residence Inn appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Torrington acquired 96-room Residence Inn in Danvers, MA for $13.5M with pre-approved conversion to 88 units.
Property located 20 miles north of Boston; JLL arranged sale and financing.
Hotel-to-multifamily conversion signals market bet on North Shore suburban demand vs. extended-stay hotel.
stories.summary: Torrington acquired the 96-room Residence Inn Boston North Shore/Danvers (51 Newbury Street) for $13.5 million with pre-approved entitlements to convert to 88 multifamily units. JLL arranged both the sale and acquisition financing. The buyer plans an initial period of continued hotel operations before executing the residential conversion.
stories.impact: Conversion of extended-stay hotel to multifamily in Danvers reflects belief that suburban Boston North Shore has stronger fundamentals for permanent residential than transient hospitality, particularly post-pandemic. This signals: (1) a potential oversupply of extended-stay product in that submarket, and (2) investor confidence in North Shore as high-barrier suburban alternative to Boston with strong residential demand. Developers should monitor Danvers and similar North Shore corridors for similar conversion/new development opportunities and population inflow drivers.

stories.title: Bonaventure Breaks Ground on $93M Development in Virginia
stories.excerpt: Bonaventure, a Virginia-based, operator-led multifamily real estate investment management firm, announced the groundbreaking of Attain at Swift Creek, a 344-unit multifamily community at 6805 Greenyard Road in Chesterfield County’s Swift Creek submarket. The $93.3 million project is financed through a 40-year, fixed-rate HUD Section 221(d)(4) loan originated by Walker & Dunlop, with Bonaventure backing the project on its balance sheet during construction, while pursuing a long-term equity partner. The community will offer a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences averaging 1,058 square feet, situated adjacent to a Kroger-anchored retail property.Attain at Swift Creek joins the growing Attain portfolio, marking the firm’s third groundbreaking of 2026, following recent groundbreakings at Attain at Greenbrier in Chesapeake and Attain at Newtown in Norfolk. Together, the three developments will deliver nearly 950 Class A apartment homes, with a combined total investment of $246.2 million across Virginia. The post Bonaventure Breaks Ground on $93M Development in Virginia appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bonaventure broke ground on 344-unit Attain at Swift Creek in Chesterfield County, Virginia for $93.3M.
Project financed via HUD 221(d)(4) 40-year fixed-rate loan from Walker & Dunlop; Bonaventure self-funding during construction.
Third Attain groundbreaking in 2026; adjacent to Kroger retail anchor signals mixed-use suburban positioning.
stories.summary: Bonaventure announced groundbreaking of Attain at Swift Creek, a 344-unit multifamily community in Chesterfield County's Swift Creek submarket near Richmond, Virginia, with total project cost of $93.3 million. The project is financed via a 40-year HUD Section 221(d)(4) fixed-rate loan from Walker & Dunlop, with Bonaventure providing interim balance-sheet funding during construction. The community includes mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units averaging 1,058 SF, adjacent to a Kroger-anchored retail property.
stories.impact: Bonaventure's third Attain groundbreaking in 2026 (Chesterfield County, Chesapeake, Greenbrier) signals aggressive expansion and execution capability in mid-Atlantic suburban markets, likely driven by population migration from urban cores and strong job growth. HUD 221(d)(4) financing indicates focus on workforce/moderate-income demographics. For developers: this demonstrates viable leverage and equity structures for suburban Virginia projects and suggests sustained demand in secondary Sunbelt metros outside major coastal cities.

stories.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Economic Impact for NYC Region Exceeds $3.3B Projection
stories.excerpt: The FIFA World Cup 2026 generated $3.5 billion in total economic impact across New York and New Jersey, exceeding the region’s original projected impact of $3.3 billion. Activity related to the tournament generated approximately $1.9 billion in direct spending, supported 27,424 total full-and part-time jobs, generated approximately $1.4 billion in total labor income and spurred $414.2 million in total state and local tax revenues, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul’s office said. For the New York/New Jersey region, FIFA World Cup 2026 activity generated $653 million in direct spending for the lodging sector. Other industries that benefited included food and beverage, which saw approximately $346 million in direct spending; retail ($246 million) and transportation ($200 million.. “Our mission was to welcome the world to New York, while making sure that every New Yorker had the chance to participate in and benefit from this once-in-a-generation event,” said Hochul. “And that’s exactly what we did. From increased spending at local businesses and restaurants to higher hotel revenues, the World Cup has left a lasting impact on our state.” The post FIFA World Cup 2026 Economic Impact for NYC Region Exceeds $3.3B Projection appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: FIFA World Cup 2026 generated $3.5B economic impact for NYC/NJ, exceeding $3.3B projection.
Lodging sector captured $653M in direct spending; food/beverage $346M; retail $246M; transportation $200M.
27,424 jobs supported; $414.2M in state/local tax revenue; event-driven visitation surge.
stories.summary: The FIFA World Cup 2026 generated $3.5 billion in total economic impact across the New York and New Jersey region, surpassing the original $3.3 billion projection. Activity spurred $1.9 billion in direct spending, supported 27,424 full- and part-time jobs, generated $1.4 billion in total labor income, and produced $414.2 million in state and local tax revenues. The lodging sector alone captured $653 million in direct spending.
stories.impact: Strong World Cup visitation and spending uplift highlights NYC region's ability to absorb transient and temporary demand, but signals limited lasting rental demand unless visitors convert to in-migration. For multifamily: monitor whether the 27,424 job-years created (food service, hospitality, logistics, retail) result in permanent employment relocations to the region. More relevant: the event's success de-risks NYC's hospitality and transit infrastructure, making it a more attractive destination for corporate relocation, which would drive sustainable long-term residential demand in Manhattan and outer boroughs.

stories.title: Waterton Acquires Rental Community in Downtown Seattle
stories.excerpt: Waterton has acquired Arrivé, a 344-unit high-rise apartment community in Seattle’s Belltown neighborhood. The acquisition includes the residential portion of the building, located on floors 11-42 above a hotel property. Waterton plans to execute a light value-add program across the residences, common areas, amenities and hallways. “Arrivé’s location in the heart of Belltown puts residents within walking distance of Seattle’s largest employers, including Amazon, Google, and Apple, along with numerous restaurants, retail options, and nearby waterfront amenities that continue to drive renter demand,” said Ben Slack, vice president of acquisitions at Waterton. Arrivé offers a mix of apartment homes, including studio, one- and two-bedroom floorplans, as well as five penthouse rental homes on the 41st floor featuring two-bedroom/two-bath and three-bedroom/three-bath configurations. The amenities at the property include a 42nd-floor lounge with conversation and cafe seating, coworking spaces and a rooftop terrace with sweeping views of the surrounding vistas. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Waterton Acquires Rental Community in Downtown Seattle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Waterton acquired Arrivé, 344-unit high-rise in Seattle's Belltown (floors 11-42 above hotel) for undisclosed price.
Property within walking distance of Amazon, Google, Apple HQ locations; mixed studio/1-bed/2-bed/penthouse units.
Waterton planning light value-add on residences, amenities, hallways; targeting tech-worker and employer-proximate demand.
stories.summary: Waterton acquired Arrivé, a 344-unit high-rise apartment community in Seattle's Belltown neighborhood, occupying floors 11-42 above a hotel property. The acquisition includes studio, one-, two-bedroom floorplans and five penthouse rental homes, with amenities including a 42nd-floor lounge, coworking spaces, and rooftop terrace. Waterton plans a light value-add program focused on residences, common areas, and amenities. The location positions residents within walking distance of major tech employers including Amazon, Google, and Apple.
stories.impact: Waterton's acquisition of Belltown high-rise signals continued confidence in Seattle's tech-employment base and premium, walkable urban submarkets despite recent Amazon office pullbacks. The employer-proximate thesis (Amazon, Google, Apple within walking distance) suggests developers should focus on Seattle neighborhoods with direct transit/walkability to major tech parks and downtown employment. Monitor: whether Amazon's return-to-office mandate and continued expansion in the region support sustained premium rental demand, or whether recent layoffs are creating supply-demand imbalances that favor value-add plays like Waterton's.

stories.title: Global Wellness Network Havas Health Expands to 254K SF at 200 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Havas Health, a global health and wellness communications network, is expanding its Midtown headquarters, Commercial Observer has learned. Havas, which creates advertising, public relations and marketing campaigns for health care brands, signed a 15-year deal to renew its existing 189,461-square-foot office at George Comfort & Sons’ 200 Madison Avenue and tack on an additional 64,657 square feet, according to the landlord. The deal, which stretches through at least 2041, brings the health company’s total footprint to 254,118 square feet across five floors of the 26-story office building seven blocks south of Grand Central Terminal. Asking rents for available office space in the building — which George Comfort owns alongside Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown — average $70 to $75 per square foot, according to ownership. Founded in 1835, Havas is one of the world’s largest global communications groups and has been a tenant at 200 Madison Avenue since the late 1990s. “Havas Health’s growing long-term commitment to 200 Madison Avenue is a testament to the appeal of the hospitality-focused, amenity-rich environment we are cultivating for our tenants,” Peter Duncan, president and CEO of George Comfort, said in a statement. “Havas has been a valued tenant for nearly three decades, and we are proud to support its next chapter of success within the tower.” Duncan and Alexander Bermingham represented ownership in-house in the deal, while Newmark’s David Falk and Jason Greenstein repped the tenant. A spokesperson for Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. George Comfort recently completed a renovation of the office tower’s entrance and lobby, and it is in the midst of building a new indoor-outdoor amenity center on the 10th floor, which will span 11,000 square feet and feature conference rooms, a game area, a lounge and event spaces. The center will also include an outdoor garden, according to the landlord. Other tenants at 200 Madison Avenue i
bullets: Havas Health renewed and expanded at 200 Madison Avenue, adding 64,657 SF to existing 189,461 SF footprint.
15-year lease through 2041; total 254,118 SF across five floors; asking rents $70-$75/SF.
Healthcare/wellness communications firm signal of Midtown office stability; long-term commitment despite secular office headwinds.
stories.summary: Havas Health, a global health and wellness communications network, signed a 15-year renewal and expansion at George Comfort & Sons' 200 Madison Avenue in Midtown, adding 64,657 square feet to its existing 189,461-square-foot footprint for a total of 254,118 square feet across five floors. The lease extends through 2041. Asking rents for available space in the 26-story building average $70–$75 per square foot.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Havas Health's long-term Midtown renewal signals modest office market stabilization in Manhattan but reflects flight to quality (trophy Class-A building near Grand Central) rather than broad office recovery. Indirectly: sustained corporate presence in Midtown supports service employment and worker housing demand, but the $70–$75/SF asking rent suggests Midtown office is still pricing in secular headwinds and not generating net job growth to drive multifamily migration.

stories.title: T30 Capital Sells East Williamsburg Loft Building at 59 Bogart Street for $30M
stories.excerpt: Local real estate investor Jo-Ann Obergfell is buying a 51-unit multifamily property in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The low-profile Obergfell, using the LLC 59 Bogart tied to an address in Brooklyn, acquired 59 Bogart Street from T30 Capital for $30 million, according to property records and seller broker CBRE. Originally an industrial property, the three-story building was converted to residential lofts in 2005. “We experienced tremendous demand for this asset as capital continues to seek value-add properties in active investment markets,” CBRE’s Robert Shapiro, who negotiated the deal alongside Ian Brooks, said in a statement. “The property attracted significant investor interest due to its transit-oriented location, recent residential conversion and proximity to major planned development projects.” Obergfell, who has served as president of Ellio’s Pizza and G.A. Productions, could not be reached for comment. She signed the deed filing as the authorized signatory of 59 Bogart LLC. Jeremy Salzberg, co-founder and managing partner of T30 Capital, signed on behalf of the firm, listing the headquarters of the firm as the mailing address for the shell corporation 59 Bogart Owner, as well as signing for two other organizations listed as under the seller. T30 Capital is linked to affiliate Sugar Hill Capital Partners, which serves as its property-owning predecessor entity and bought 59 Bogart Street — also known as 315 Seigel Street — for $39.5 million in 2016. All new business, investments and operations are conducted directly through T30 Capital. The property situated above the L train’s Morgan Avenue station offers one- to three-bedroom units, along with a lounge, a gym, a bike room and communal outdoor spaces for residents, according to CBRE. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Jo-Ann Obergfell acquired 59 Bogart Street, East Williamsburg, 51-unit loft building for $30M via 59 Bogart LLC.
Three-story building converted to residential lofts in 2005; valued for transit location and proximity to planned development.
Buyer is local investor/operator; CBRE noted strong demand for value-add residential in active Brooklyn markets.
stories.summary: Local investor Jo-Ann Obergfell, via 59 Bogart LLC, acquired 59 Bogart Street in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn—a 51-unit residential loft building—from T30 Capital for $30 million. The three-story building was converted to residential in 2005. CBRE brokers noted the asset attracted significant investor interest due to its transit-oriented location, recent residential conversion history, and proximity to major planned development projects in the neighborhood.
stories.impact: East Williamsburg value-add acquisition highlights ongoing capital demand for transit-adjacent, conversion-eligible multifamily in Brooklyn, particularly near planned development corridors. The $30M price for 51 units (~$588K per unit) reflects robust investor appetite and limited value-add supply in the submarket. For developers: this signals opportunity to identify additional industrial/loft conversion candidates in East Williamsburg and adjacent Brooklyn neighborhoods (Bushwick, Ridgewood) before planned transit/mixed-use projects compress availability and lift values further.

stories.title: Savills Inks 20K-SF Deal at Rudin’s 560 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: The deal-makers at Savills have struck a lease of their own. The global real estate advisory firm is expanding its New York City presence by taking 20,481 square feet for a satellite office at Rudin’s 560 Lexington Avenue, according to a Thursday announcement by the landlord. Savills will occupy the entire third floor at the 22-story Midtown East tower for a five-year term. Asking rent for the deal was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for Midtown office space was $84.88 per square foot in July, according to Colliers. Rudin’s Kevin Daly and Craig Panzirer represented the landlord in-house in the deal, alongside a CBRE team of Brett Shannon, Peter Turchin, Eric Deutsch, Lauren Levy and Jacob Rosenthal. Savills represented itself in the transaction. Savills’ new office space sits four blocks north of its U.S. headquarters at 399 Park Avenue. The new lease will accommodate Savills’ program and project management group, a spokesperson for the brokerage told Commercial Observer. The added elbow room comes just a few weeks after Savills completed its acquisition and launch of Eastdil Secured Savills in a major platform expansion. Situated at the corner of East 50th Street and Lexington Avenue three blocks east of Rockefeller Center, 560 Lexington has attracted more than 110,000 square feet of deals that have now been completed there this year, according to BXP. Hedge fund SummitTX Capital took nearly 18,000 square feet across the 19th floor earlier this year, Commercial Observer reported, followed by investment firm Ally Bridge Group’s 6,440-square-foot relocation in May, financial firm Marex’s 39,552-square-foot deal in April, and sports investment firm Dynasty Equity’s 9,910-square-foot lease in June. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Savills leased 20,481 SF entire third floor at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue (Midtown East) for five years.
Tenant taking satellite office for program/project management group; located four blocks from Savills US HQ.
Lease rent not disclosed; Midtown office average asking ~$84.88/SF; signals minor office market activity.
stories.summary: Savills, the global real estate advisory firm, leased 20,481 square feet—the entire third floor—at Rudin Company's 560 Lexington Avenue in Midtown East for a five-year term. The space will house Savills' program and project management group, located four blocks north of the firm's U.S. headquarters at 399 Park Avenue. Asking rent was not disclosed, though Midtown average asking rent was approximately $84.88 per square foot in July.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance. Savills' expansion is a single-tenant, intra-firm backfill for project/program management functions—not a signal of broad office recovery or population inflow to Midtown East. It reflects real estate service consolidation near headquarters rather than job creation or residential demand drivers.

stories.title: Vivmark Residential Acquires California Multifamily Portfolio for $742M
stories.excerpt: Following a generational merger, the largest apartment real estate investment trust (REIT) in the business just got a little bit bigger. Days after AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential completed their $71 billion merger — the largest merger of publicly traded REITs in history — the new firm, Vivmark Residential, has acquired seven apartment complexes in Northern California near San Francisco, totaling more than 1,800 units, in several transactions totaling $741.8 million. The Mercury News first reported the sales to Vivmark Residential, a public entity that now boasts a portfolio in excess of 180,000 rental apartment units. The acquisitions are spread out over seven deals. Vivmark acquired Avalon Campbell, a 348-unit complex at 508 Railway Avenue in Campbell, Calif., for $147.3 million; Avalon Towers on the Peninsula, a 238-unit complex at 2400 West El Camino Real in Mountain View, Calif., for $140.4 million; Avalon Fremont, a 308-unit complex at 39939 Stevenson Common in Fremont, Calif., for $124.3 million; Eaves Creekside, a 300-unit apartment at 151 Calderon Avenue in Mountain View, Calif., for $117.3 million; Eaves Fremont, a 237-unit complex at 231 Woodcreek Common in Fremont for $88.9 million; Eaves Dublin, a 204-unit apartment at 7904 Fall Creek Road in Dublin, Calif., for $64.6 million; and Eaves Union City, a 208-unit complex at 2175 Decoto Road in Union City, Calif., for $59.1 million. Brad Dillman, founder and principal of Florey Street Advisors, told CO after the merger was announced that both AvalonBay and Equity had “enormous coastal exposure across both firms,” and that “they overlap in like 95 percent of their geographies.” The move to buy seven buildings in the Northern California Bay Area emphasizes that coastal thesis. “Either group might have merged with Camden [Property Trust], which has Sun Belt exposure,” said Dillman. “But they decided to double down on the coasts.” Vivmark Residential did not respond to requests for comment. bullets: Post-merger Vivmark Residential acquired seven Northern California apartment complexes, 1,800+ units for $741.8M.
Portfolio includes Avalon Campbell (348 units, $147.3M), Avalon Towers Peninsula (238 units, $140.4M), Avalon Fremont (308 units, $124.3M).
Vivmark (AvalonBay + Equity Residential merger, 180K+ units nationwide) executing strategic consolidation in Bay Area.
stories.summary: Vivmark Residential—formed following the $71 billion merger of AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential, the largest public REIT merger in history—acquired seven apartment complexes in Northern California near San Francisco totaling more than 1,800 units across multiple transactions valued at $741.8 million. Acquisitions include Avalon Campbell (348 units, $147.3M), Avalon Towers on the Peninsula (238 units, $140.4M), and Avalon Fremont (308 units, $124.3M). Vivmark now operates a portfolio exceeding 180,000 rental apartment units.
stories.impact: Post-merger REIT consolidation signals capital availability and strategic conviction in Bay Area multifamily despite regional tech volatility and high construction costs. Vivmark's rapid deployment of merger-related capital into Bay Area acquisitions (likely at stabilized cap rates) suggests: (1) compressed pricing in secondary/tertiary Bay Area markets (Campbell, Mountain View, Fremont), (2) belief in long-term demand from tech employment and population density, and (3) opportunity for smaller developers to acquire newer assets in San Francisco, Oakland, and Silicon Valley before mega-REITs further consolidate supply. Monitor Vivmark's execution timeline and any capital redeployment signals.
